How to reach your target speed

Two people can score 26 WPM and need different exercises. Start with your accuracy, then look at the gap to your target. Use the same timer and practice category when comparing results.

26 WPM with 88% accuracy

Start with a missed word. Suppose the passage says “quiet” and you type “quite.” Watch the order of the last two letters. Type “quiet” slowly once, then type it again at your usual pace. In the next timed passage, see whether the same swap returns. A lower speed with fewer repeated mistakes is useful progress in this exercise.

26 WPM with 98% accuracy

For a 30 WPM target, you need 150 correct characters in a minute. At 26 WPM you produce about 130. The gap is 20 characters per minute, or five every 15 seconds. Try reading the next word while your fingers finish the current one. Use a fresh one-minute passage and see whether shorter pauses increase speed while preserving accuracy.

Fast for one minute, slower for three

Do one three-minute trial at a comfortable pace. Notice whether errors appear near the end or around a particular kind of text. If punctuation interrupts you throughout the test, use the punctuation category. If errors gather late, try a steadier opening minute. Compare another three-minute run before changing your target.

Read your mistake breakdown

Each reached character position counts once. Correcting a comma with Backspace improves the finished text, while the breakdown keeps the first attempt. The focused drill targets the group with the most first-try mistakes. Its follow-up uses different text and shows correct attempts out of all reached positions in that group. Compare both fractions: one correct comma out of one is weaker evidence than ten out of ten.

How to use History

Compare your last three sessions in the same category and duration. If only one unusually familiar passage took you above target, try again on fresh text. Keep missed-word drill results separate from ordinary passage results because the drill repeats a smaller set of words.
